chunks: And in it is that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say in his supplication: O Allah, I ask You by Your Greatest Name, which when called upon is answered, and when asked for is given.
And he said: O Allah, I ask You by Your Name which He sent to Gabriel to convey to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and he said: O Muhammad, this is the Greatest Name of Allah.
So he said: O Gabriel, what is it? He said: It is Allah. He said: O Muhammad, indeed Allah the Exalted has named Himself Allah, so ask Him by it.
So he said: O Allah, I ask You by Your Greatest Name, which when called upon is answered, and when asked for is given.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّم: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What is the Greatest Name of Allah in Shia tradition and how is it used in supplication?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to establish the theological efficacy of the *Ism Allah al-A'zam* (Greatest Name) as a direct conduit for divine response, a concept central to Shia esoteric interpretation (*ta'wil*) of supplication. This teaching underscores the belief that specific divine attributes, when invoked with certainty, transcend ordinary prayer mechanics, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on the spiritual potency of Allah's names in achieving *istijabah* (acceptance).
